notes.body:
Whole-body model of omeprazole
PBPK/PD model of omeprazole with its enantiomers S-omeprazole and R-omeprazole, their metabolism in the liver by CYP2C19 and CYP3A4, the renal and biliary excretion of the metabolites, the absorption of the application forms and the inhibition of the gastric proton pumps.
The content of this model has been carefully created in a manual research effort.

body.p: GFR per renal blood flow (76.3 ml/l). Calibrated so that the healthy GFR is 101 ml/min at the renal blood flow of 1.32354 l/min of 75 kg, the normal GFR of the classes of renal impairment (pkpdsim.impairment).
The GFR of healthy kidneys, which scales with the renal blood flow and so with the body weight; the GFR is KI__f_renal_function times this rate.

Exchange flow between the plasma and the tissues at the reference body weight BW_ref, the same for the enantiomers and the metabolites (not identifiable separately). Fast, not fitted: the IV curves show no distribution phase and every fit ran to the upper bound (50 and 200 l/min); the partition Kp_ome gives the volume.
Vss 0.17-0.30 l/kg (Regaardh1990), 0.14-0.37 l/kg (Andersson1990a, Regaardh1986); omeprazole is 95 % bound to plasma proteins.
The value of Kp_ome is the result of the fit PK_20261020_090631__aa2cf, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.
